results.title: Phone Storage
results.text:
This page is for Andronix with **Termux**, on phones that can't run Linux in the app (Android 7, or no 64-bit ARM processor), or if you use the command-line installer. For Linux in the app, see [Android files in Linux](/use/android-files).

This page is for Linux in Termux. For distros you installed in the app, see [Android files in Linux](/use/android-files).

This page shows how to reach your phone's internal storage from inside your Linux distro. On distros from Andronix 2.0, it's one command in Termux.

results.title: Back Up Your Files
results.text:
There's no backup for distros in the app yet. To keep your files, copy them out: your Linux home shows in Android's **Files** app under **Andronix**, and you can save files to `~/Android/Download` or `~/Android/Documents` in Linux, which appear in **Download/Andronix** and **Documents/Andronix** on your phone. See [Android files in Linux](/use/android-files).

You can bring a backup from Termux **into** the app: see [Move a distro from Termux into the app](/install/standalone-and-termux#move-a-distro-from-termux-into-the-app).

For distros in Termux, `andronix backup` saves the whole distro: see [Back up and restore in Termux](/termux/backups).

Keep it updated:

results.title: Android Files in Linux
results.text:
Two folders are shared between Android and Linux:

| In Linux | On your device |
|---|---|
| `~/Android/Download` | **Download/Andronix** |
| `~/Android/Documents` | **Documents/Andronix** |

What you save in those folders in Linux appears in Android right away, for example in the Files app, a gallery or an email app. Each distro has a `~/Android/README.txt` that says the same.

- **Android 11 and newer:** no permission is needed.
- **Android 8 to 10:** the app asks for the storage permission the first time. If you said no, tap **Allow** on the screen, or allow it in Android's settings.

Only these two folders are shared. The rest of your phone's storage isn't visible inside Linux.

**Android 11 and newer:** files that *other apps* put in Download/Andronix (or Documents/Andronix) aren't visible to Linux, and neither are files from before you reinstalled Andronix. Use **Import** or **Send to Linux** for those (below).

results.title: Requirements
results.text:
The first time, the app runs a short self-check (about a tenth of a second) to make sure Linux can run inside it on your device. It runs again after each app update.

If your device can't run Linux in the app, the app says so when you pick a distro, and installs it in Termux instead. For example: **Linux in the app isn't available on this phone (Needs Android 8 or newer), so Andronix uses Termux.** The reason in brackets is one of these:

| The app says | What it means |
|---|---|
| Needs a device with a 64-bit ARM processor. | Your device's main processor isn't arm64. Use Termux. |
| Needs Android 8 or newer. | Your device runs Android 7. Use Termux. |
| Linux can't run in the app on this device. | The self-check failed. Use Termux, and please [report it](/troubleshooting/in-the-app#report-a-problem). |
| Not available right now; new installs use Termux. | We've switched standalone mode off for new installs while we fix a problem. Distros you already installed in the app still open. |
| Paused while we fix a problem. | We've paused standalone mode. Your distros and files stay on your device, and Termux still works. |

results.title: The andronix Command
results.text:
installer 2.0.1+

```bash
andronix doctor [<distro>]
```

Shows what Andronix knows about your phone, and what it adjusts for it:

- **This phone:** the Linux kernel, the Android version and ROM, the Termux build, RAM and free space, and whether Android's phantom process killer is on (see [Process completed (signal 9)](/troubleshooting/signal-9)).
- **Syscalls under proot:** how a few system calls behave inside a distro on this phone. It tests inside the distro you name, or the first one installed; with no distro installed, this part is skipped.
- **Fixes that apply:** the compatibility fixes Andronix uses on this phone, each with the reason. They're applied automatically when you install, resume or update a distro; `doctor` only reports them.

It changes nothing, and it checks again each time you run it. When you ask for help, include its output, or paste it into the app's [Report a problem](/troubleshooting/report-a-problem) form.

results.title: The Desktop in Termux:X11
results.text:
**Get the Termux:X11 APK:** it's published only on the Termux project's GitHub. Open the [nightly release](https://github.com/termux/termux-x11/releases/tag/nightly) and download **`termux-x11-universal-debug.apk`**, which works on every processor. Andronix doesn't host or mirror it. Then follow [Set it up once](#set-it-up-once).

This page is for Andronix with **Termux**, on phones that can't run Linux in the app (Android 7, or no 64-bit ARM processor), or if you use the command-line installer. Termux:X11 itself needs Android 8 or newer; on Android 7, use [VNC](/termux/vnc). For Linux in the app, see [The desktop in the app](/desktop/in-the-app).

Termux:X11 is an Android app that shows your distro's desktop full screen on the phone, at the phone's own resolution. There's nothing to connect to and no desktop password to type: one command in Termux opens it.

results.title: Requirements
results.text:
On a phone with Android 7 or without a 64-bit ARM processor (x86, or 32-bit ARM), Andronix runs Linux inside Termux instead. What those phones need: [Requirements for Termux](/termux/requirements).

Install in the app:

results.title: Requirements
results.text: Andronix runs Linux in the app on most Android phones and tablets from the last several years. Check these before you install.

results.title: Limitations
results.text:
Distros you install in the app have the same proot limits as above, plus:

- **One distro runs at a time.**
- **No microphone** yet; sound output works.
- **No backup inside the app** yet. See [Back up and restore](/use/backups).
- **No VNC from another device.** The desktop shows in the app only. In Termux, [VNC](/termux/vnc) still works.
- **SSH isn't supported** in 10.1. See [SSH](/termux/ssh).
- **arm64 with Android 8 or newer only**; other devices use Termux. See [Requirements](/start-here/requirements).

results.title: Requirements for Termux
results.text:
This page is for Andronix with Termux, on phones that can't run Linux in the app (Android 7, or no 64-bit ARM processor). For everything else, see [Requirements](/start-here/requirements).

In Termux, Andronix runs on more devices than in the app, including Android 7, 32-bit ARM, x86 and x86_64:

| | Command line only | With a desktop |
|---|---|---|
| **Android** | 7 or newer | 7 or newer |
| **CPU** | arm64 (most phones), also arm, x86 and x86_64 for some distros | Same |
| **Free storage** | about 0.5 GB | 1.5 to 2 GB (about 3 GB for KDE Plasma) |
| **RAM** | 2 GB | 3 GB or more is comfortable; 4 GB or more for KDE Plasma |
| **Root** | Not needed | Not needed |

results.title: Linux in the App: Limits and Problems
results.text:
- **arm64 and Android 8 or newer only.** Other devices use Termux. See [Requirements](/start-here/requirements).
- **Sound plays, but there's no microphone** yet.
- **The first install takes 5 to 30 minutes.** It keeps going in the background with the **Linux is running** notification.
- **One distro runs at a time.**
- **Android 11 and newer:** Linux can't see files that other apps put in Download/Andronix. Use **Import** or **Send to Linux**. See [Android files in Linux](/use/android-files).
- **Firefox says its security sandbox is disabled.** That's needed for Linux to run inside the app; Firefox can still only reach what Android lets the app reach.
- **GPU acceleration is experimental,** and can be slower on fast devices. See [GPU acceleration](/use/gpu).
- **Safe mode can remove window title bars.** See [Black screen and safe mode](/troubleshooting/black-screen).
- **Home-screen shortcuts need a launcher that supports them.** Most do; we tested Pixel and Samsung. See [Linux apps on your home screen](/use/shortcuts).

results.title: Requirements
results.text: On devices with a Linux kernel older than 4.8 (some Android 8 and 9 phones), the app doesn't offer XFCE, MATE or KDE Plasma in the app, because they stay black there: it says **Needs Linux kernel 4.8 or newer. On this device, use LXQt.** LXQt and the command line work. Modded OS needs kernel 4.8 or newer. In Termux, desktops install but may stay black; see [The installer warns about an old kernel](/termux/install-problems#the-installer-warns-about-an-old-kernel).

data.delta: In the app you need an arm64 phone with Android 8 or newer.
